communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Outside Counsel Billing Invoices (Simmons Sweeney Freimund Smith Tardif PLLC)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

A specific set of public financial ledger and vendor records. The context and specific litigation parameters for this request are derived directly from the District’s document production under MuckRock Request #R000266-120625 (specifically File: 2023-01-13T170551.000Z_1506_Redacted), regarding the civil litigation defended on behalf of the District before Judge McHale by attorney Bret Simmons. Because the District has already processed and verified the background communications involving this outside counsel, locating these public expenditure records requires zero extended search time.

RECORDS REQUESTED: Any and all finalized corporate billing invoices, line-item fee summaries, or retainers submitted to the District by Simmons Sweeney Freimund Smith Tardif PLLC (aka SSS Law Group) between November 1, 2022, and June 30, 2023, for defense work regarding the litigation before Judge McHale referenced under Smokeball ID: e1876dd9-7dad-4690-8b96-16ab2e1c248d.

LIMITATION OF SCOPE & REDACTION CLAUSE: To maximize administrative efficiency and minimize any review burdens on District staff, the requester explicitly pre-excludes and waives any interest in the Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of any individual student, parent, or family member under FERPA.Processing Instruction: Please do not withhold these corporate billing records in full. Pursuant to standard Washington public spending rules, apply a localized blackout exclusively to protected student names, while releasing the full descriptions of hours billed, attorney hourly rates, and macro public funds disbursed to outside counsel.

PRA Statutory Compliance Reminder:As provided by RCW 42.56.520, a response is required within five (5) business days. Because this request targets localized vendor legal billing files thoroughly identified via Request #R000266-120625, extensive multi-month database searches are unnecessary.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Kung Fu Joe

title: Retail food facility roster and inspection data (Ventura County, CA)

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Retail food facility roster and inspection data (Ventura County, CA)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

To the Records Officer, Ventura County Environmental Health Division (Resource Management Agency):

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act (Gov. Code § 7920.000 et seq.), I request copies of the following records in electronic format:

1. The current roster of all active retail food facility permits maintained by your agency, including for each facility, to the extent maintained: facility name and DBA, site address, mailing address, owner or operator name, phone number, permit type or program/risk classification, and permit status with effective dates.

2. Retail food facility inspection results from 2024-08-06 through the date this request is processed, including for each inspection: the facility identifier or name and address, inspection date, inspection type, score or grade where used, and the violation codes and descriptions cited.

Both categories are maintained in your environmental health data system and are routinely produced by comparable agencies as spreadsheet exports. Per Gov. Code § 7922.575, I request the records in any electronic format in which they already exist — CSV, Excel, or a database export is preferred over PDF, and no new record needs to be created to comply.

If any portion of a record is exempt, please release the remainder with the exempt portion redacted (§ 7922.525) and cite the specific exemption relied upon. If duplication fees apply, please provide an itemized estimate of the direct cost of duplication in advance (§ 7922.530); for electronic records we expect this to be minimal or zero.

Thank you for your assistance.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Benjamin Conn

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Specifically, I am requesting: 

All proposals and responses submitted by all vendors. 

All existing contracts, agreements, amendments, addenda, and pricing schedules resulting from this solicitation. 

All evaluation materials, including scoring sheets, evaluation committee notes or summaries, and recommendation memoranda. 

All bid tabulations, comparison matrices, or award justifications. 

All addenda to the solicitation, and any questions and answers (Q&A) or clarifications issued to vendors. 

Any other documentation or correspondence (including emails, letters, or internal memoranda) material to the evaluation, selection, and award of this stop-arm camera enforcement program. 

If any portion of the requested records is exempt from disclosure, please provide the non-exempt portions and cite the specific statutory basis for each withholding or redaction.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jon Smith

title: Flock Safety ALPR Use Across Union County, NJ — Audit Logs, Searches & Data Sharing (Municipal Clerk)

communications.subject: New Jersey Open Public Records Act Request: Flock Safety ALPR Use Across Union County, NJ — Audit Logs, Searches & Data Sharing (Municipal Clerk)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New Jersey Open Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

For the period July 20, 2026 through August 19, 2026, please provide:

1. Records showing the total number of license plates, vehicle detections, or plate reads captured or scanned through Flock Safety ALPR systems accessible to or operated by the department.

2. The names of all hot lists, watch lists, alert lists, or similar lists used, enabled, or accessible through the department’s Flock Safety system.

3. A list of all law enforcement agencies, government entities, organizations, or other entities with which the department shares Flock Safety ALPR data.

4. A list of all law enforcement agencies, government entities, organizations, or other entities from which the department receives or has access to Flock Safety ALPR data.

5. All agreements, memoranda of understanding, contracts, arrangements, or other records concerning access to Flock Safety cameras, systems, or data owned, funded, or operated by homeowner associations, private businesses, private organizations, or individuals.

6. All current contracts, memoranda of understanding, agreements, amendments, renewals, statements of work, or similar agreements between the department, municipality, or other applicable public entity and Flock Safety.

7. All procurement records related to Flock Safety, including purchase orders, invoices, bids, quotes, proposals, requisitions, payment records, and records reflecting the purchase, lease, subscription, acquisition, installation, or renewal of Flock Safety equipment or services.

8. All audit logs, search logs, query logs, usage reports, or similar records relating to the department’s use of Flock Safety ALPR systems during the requested period, including but not limited to:

- Records of license plate or vehicle searches performed by agency personnel;
- Dates and timestamps of searches;
- User identification associated with searches, including names, badge numbers, usernames, or user IDs, where maintained;
- Case numbers, incident numbers, investigation references, reasons, or purposes associated with searches, where maintained;
- Records showing networks or agencies whose Flock data is shared with or accessible to the department;
- Records showing networks or agencies to which the department shares its Flock data;
- Event logs, system activity logs, or audit records reflecting changes to hot lists, watch lists, alerts, users, permissions, or network-sharing settings;
- Records showing changes to data-sharing relationships or network access; and
- Records reflecting live-stream, live-view, camera access, or similar access permissions and configuration settings, if applicable.

This request specifically includes records available through Flock Safety features or reports identified as “Organization Audit,” “Network Audit,” or equivalent audit, usage, sharing, or administrative reports available within the Flock Safety platform, including the “Insights” section where applicable.

9. Records showing the department’s current Flock Safety network-sharing configuration, including which networks, agencies, or organizations share data with the department and which networks, agencies, or organizations receive data from the department.

10. Screenshots, exports, reports, or other existing records reflecting relevant Flock Safety configuration settings, including network-sharing settings and live-stream/live-view access settings, to the extent such records are maintained by the agency.

Please provide responsive records in their original electronic format where reasonably available. For databases, audit logs, search logs, reports, or tabular records, I prefer CSV, XLS/XLSX, or another native machine-readable format rather than PDF printouts.

This request seeks existing government records and does not require the agency to create a new record. If a requested list or summary does not exist as a standalone record, please provide the existing report, export, audit log, configuration record, or other record containing the requested information.

In advance of filing this request, Flock Safety was consulted regarding the availability of these records. Flock Safety indicated that if an agency administrator has difficulty locating relevant audit or system records, the administrator may contact Flock Safety for support.

If any portion of a responsive record is considered exempt from disclosure, please redact only the exempt portion and provide the remainder of the record. Please identify the specific legal basis for each withholding or redaction.

The requested records will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

Thank you for your assistance.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Madthew Pierre-Louis

title: Library Contract Request: EBSCO Academic Search Premier (College Of Southern Nevada)

communications.subject: Nevada Public Records Act Request: Library Contract Request: EBSCO Academic Search Premier (College Of Southern Nevada)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Nevada Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1) The most recent contract, governing, base, or master license agreement with EBSCO, relating to the product Academic Search Premier;
2) All related terms and conditions, terms of service, amendments, addenda, appendices, attachments, product terms, MOUs, MOAs, data processing agreements, and/or letters of intent; and
3) All financial documents or records of financial transactions, exchanges or obligations related to contractual relations with EBSCO for Academic Search Premier. 

Please do not limit your search to strictly direct agreements or renewals between the institution and EBSCO, but include all agreements and related documentation through consortia such as a state or regional library consortium (such as the Greater Western Library Alliance) or Lyrasis.

Responsive materials include all contracts, agreements, amendments, appendices, invoices, and any other documents listed above that incorporate language governing terms of use of Academic Search Premier.

We are an alliance of academic research librarians conducting critical research on library vendor contract terminology related to data privacy to identify and expose significant disparities in language between vendors and institutions. This research is essential for advancing national awareness and advocacy around library patron data privacy rights. We would be grateful for your cooperation in supporting this important initiative.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Ellen Dubinsky

Good Morning.  We received the results for the e-mail search you requested and the results captured 5340 e-mails.  Based on a very quick review, it appears that the term “contract” is the source of many of the hits.  There are also many closed records in the results – for instance e-mails from the department’s medical contract monitor team that contain health information on individual offenders.  With the press of other business, this review will take some time so I thought it might be prudent to ask if you would want to remove “contract” from the search terms to narrow the results.   I hope that makes sense and if you would like us to review all the results as the request was submitted, we will certainly do that.

If you have any questions, please let me know.

Sincerely,


Matt Briesacher
Office of the General Counsel

Missouri Department of Corrections
2729 Plaza Drive
Jefferson City, MO 65109

title: US Navy support for NASCAR 2026 San Diego Weekend

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: US Navy support for NASCAR 2026 San Diego Weekend
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All documents pertaining to collaboration between the US Navy and the TV production of NASCAR 2026 San Diego Weekend. Such documents may include but should not be limited to: script notes; production assistance agreements; photographs; and all records of communications between employees of the Navy and members of the cast, crew, and production company of NASCAR 2026 San Diego Weekend, including memos, notes of meetings and conference calls, emails, and other forms of communication.

NASCAR 2026 San Diego Weekend appears (as "NASCAR 2026 San Diego Weekend [Amazon Prime streaming, FS1 network and CW network]") in a list of Navy-supported productions for the year 2025 that was released to me through FOIA. That list is attached to this request.

I am the Director of Research Operations at a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization called The Decoding Culture Foundation as well as the editor-in-chief and a contributor to a research magazine published by said foundation titled "Cultural Engineering Studies." These documents will be used for public education and research purposes. I therefore request a waiver of all fees that may otherwise apply. Attached is a document with organization letterhead confirming my position, as well as the organization's 501(c)(3) application and approval form.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Brett Carollo

Dear Mr. Carollo: 

The Department of the Navy received your Freedom of Information (FOIA) / Privacy Act (PA) request dated 4 May 2026 and placed it in queue for processing by order of receipt on 4 May 2026. 

Unusual circumstances arise when a response within the statutory 20-day period may not be attainable due to: 

1. Collection and search for records from a facility outside of this office. 
2. Volume of records that may be responsive to your request. 
3. Consultation with one or more agencies having a substantial interest in the determination or the subject matter. 

The Navy FOIA program is decentralized, requiring our office to search and gather documents from Navy component offices which are not geographically co-located. Per the Department of the Navy FOIA/PA regulation 32 CFR §701.8(g)(2), this office grants itself an extension of ten days response time. We appreciate your patience and understand the importance of timely responses to FOIA requests and apologize for any inconvenience this delay may cause. 

Additionally, please be aware that the U.S. Navy’s new FOIA portal, Secure Release, is online. For your convenience, you may now submit FOIA requests online at www.SecureRelease.us or www.FOIA.gov.

title: City of Glenpool Opioid Settlement Funds

communications.subject: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: City of Glenpool Opioid Settlement Funds
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Under the Oklahoma Open Records Act, 51 §24A.1 et seq., I request an opportunity to inspect or obtain copies of public records related to the allocation and use of opioid lawsuit settlement funds in the City of Glenpool. Specifically, I am seeking:

1. Documentation of the amount of opioid settlement funds your office has received thus far from the Oklahoma Attorney General’s Office as a non-litigating political subdivision. 
2. Records detailing which individuals and/or programs have been awarded a portion of your opioid lawsuit settlement funds. 
3. Any documentation related to the review or approval process to apply for funding, including the names and organizations of individuals involved in the application process. 
4. Minutes of any public meetings or hearings, including public officials, in which opioid settlement fund allocation was discussed. 
5. Any correspondence and attachments between county officials regarding the allocation or use of these funds. 

If there are any fees for searching or copying these records, please inform me if the cost will exceed $25.00. However, I would also like to request a waiver of all fees, as disclosure of the requested information is in the public interest. This request is related to news-gathering purposes; it is not being sought for commercial purposes.

If you expect a significant delay in responding to or in fulfilling this request, please contact me with information about when I might expect copies or the ability to inspect the requested records.

I look forward to receiving your response to this request. Thank you for the help, and please let me know if you have any questions. 

Sincerely, 

Sierra Pfeifer | KOSU
Mental health & addiction reporter
sierra@kosu.org | 919-448-5430

title: Information Regarding RCW 9.94A.030 §36 (Department of Corrections)

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Information Regarding RCW 9.94A.030 §36 (Department of Corrections)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Unless otherwise specified, I am requesting data covering the five-year period through the date of this request.

For purposes of this request, "gang enhancement" refers to the sentencing enhancement applied under RCW 9.94A.533(8) to offenses qualifying as "criminal street gang-related offenses" as defined in RCW 9.94A.030(14), involving defendants qualifying as "criminal street gang associates or members" as defined in RCW 9.94A.030(13), and involving a "pattern of criminal street gang activity" as defined in RCW 9.94A.030(36).
1. The total number of individuals charged with a criminal street gang-related offense under RCW 9.94A.030(14), or against whom a gang sentencing enhancement under RCW 9.94A.533(8) was alleged, broken down by year for the past five years.
2. The racial and gender demographics of all individuals charged with a criminal street gang-related offense or gang enhancement under the above provisions during that period, disaggregated by year to the extent available.
3. Conviction rates for individuals charged with a gang-related offense or against whom a gang enhancement was alleged, including the number and percentage of cases resolved by conviction, acquittal, dismissal, or other disposition, broken down by year.
4. The number of individuals currently in Washington Department of Corrections (DOC) custody whose sentence includes a gang enhancement imposed under RCW 9.94A.533(8).
5. The number of cases over the past five years in which a gang enhancement under RCW 9.94A.533(8) was included in the initial charging or sentencing documentation but was subsequently not imposed as part of a negotiated plea or sentencing agreement, broken down by year.
6. The average sentence length in cases where a gang enhancement under RCW 9.94A.533(8) was dropped or reduced through a plea or sentencing agreement, compared with the average sentence length in cases where the enhancement was imposed at sentencing, broken down by year to the extent available.
7. The age distribution — including mean age, median age, and full age range — of individuals charged with a gang-related offense or against whom a gang enhancement was alleged under the above provisions, over the past five years.
8. The average total sentence length for the underlying predicate offense alone, compared with the average total sentence for the underlying offense combined with the gang enhancement under RCW 9.94A.533(8), for cases resolved during the past five years.
9. The number of cases in which a gang enhancement under RCW 9.94A.533(8) was applied involving: (a) juveniles tried as adults in superior court following a decline hearing under RCW 13.40.110; or (b) defendants whose cases originated in juvenile court proceedings under Title 13 RCW, over the past five years.
10. For defendants against whom a gang enhancement under RCW 9.94A.533(8) was alleged over the past five years: the number represented by the Office of Public Defense or county public defender versus private counsel, along with corresponding conviction rates and average sentence lengths for each group.
11. The number of gang enhancement cases under RCW 9.94A.533(8) prosecuted by county, broken down by year, for the past five years.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jenny Wadhwa

title: Contract Request: Interfolio (Western Washington University)

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Contract Request: Interfolio (Western Washington University)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

The most recent contract, governing, base, or master license agreement with Elsevier relating to the licensing of Interfolio;
All related terms and conditions, terms of service, amendments, addenda, appendices, attachments, product terms, MOUs, MOAs, and/or data processing agreements; 
All financial documents or records of financial transactions, exchanges or obligations related to the contractual relations with Elsevier for faculty information system technology;
and
Assessment documentation such as the Higher Education Community Vendor Assessment Toolkit (HECVAT) related to Interfolio. 

Responsive materials include all contracts, agreements, amendments, appendices, invoices, and any other documents listed above that incorporate language governing terms of use of Interfolio.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Michele Gibney

title: Town Take‑Home Vehicles and Taxable Fringe Benefits

communications.subject: New York Freedom of Information Law Request: Town Take‑Home Vehicles and Taxable Fringe Benefits
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New York Freedom of Information Law, I hereby request the following records:

Copies of records from January 1, 2022 through the present relating to town‑owned vehicles assigned to employees as take‑home or personally assigned vehicles.
Please provide the following categories of records, in any format in which they are maintained (paper or electronic), and from any department that maintains them:

Vehicle assignments
*Any lists, inventories, or other records identifying town‑owned vehicles assigned to individual employees for take‑home or personally assigned use, including: vehicle year/make/model, VIN, department, and the name and title of the assigned employee, with dates of assignment and, if applicable, return or reassignment.

Usage / mileage records
*Any records showing the odometer reading or total accumulated mileage for each town‑owned vehicle assigned as a take‑home or personally assigned vehicle, as of the most recent date available.
*Mileage logs, trip sheets, vehicle use logs, GPS/telematics reports, or similar records showing business, commuting, or other personal use of those vehicles.
*Any forms or reports employees submit to document personal or commuting use of employer‑provided vehicles for payroll or tax purposes.

Payroll / taxable fringe benefit records
*Payroll, accounting, or other records that show taxable fringe benefit amounts attributed to employees’ personal or commuting use of town‑owned take‑home vehicles and included in their wages, such as payroll registers, year‑to‑date taxable fringe benefit totals, W‑2 support, or similar records.
*Any records indicating the method used to value this fringe benefit (for example, cents‑per‑mile, annual lease value, or commuting valuation), consistent with IRS Publication 15‑B or related IRS guidance on employer‑provided vehicles.

Policies and reviews
*Any written policies, procedures, or internal guidance on the assignment, use, or personal/commuting use of town‑owned vehicles.
*Any audit reports, management letters, or internal reviews since January 1, 2022 that address take‑home vehicles, vehicle use recordkeeping, or reporting of taxable fringe benefits for employer‑provided vehicles.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Michael McCall

title: PitchBook Data FOIA Request: City of Kissimmee Municipal Firefighters' Retirement Plan

communications.subject: Florida Sunshine Law Request: PitchBook Data FOIA Request: City of Kissimmee Municipal Firefighters' Retirement Plan
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Florida Sunshine Law, I hereby request the following records:

I am currently seeking updated quarterly performance data from your plan’s alternative asset holdings for the following date(s): 1Q20, 2Q20, 3Q20, 4Q20, 1Q21, 2Q21, 3Q21, 4Q21, 1Q26 & 2Q26.
As always, thank you in advance for taking the time to send the requested documents. Below is the formal request.
On behalf of PitchBook Data, Inc., under The Florida Sunshine Law, I request a copy of the quarterly public records from 1Q20, 2Q20, 3Q20, 4Q20, 1Q21, 2Q21, 3Q21, 4Q21, 1Q26 & 2Q26 for the following information, preferably in Excel or PDF format.
1.	Names and vintage years of all private equity, venture capital, mezzanine, distressed, real estate/REIT, debt and infrastructure partnerships in City of Kissimmee Municipal Firefighters' Retirement Plan's portfolio.
2.	Commitments made to each partnership.
3.	Contributions drawn down since inception.
4.	Distributions made to City of Kissimmee Municipal Firefighters' Retirement Plan to date by each individual partnership.
5.	Net Asset Value of each partnership.
6.	Internal rates of return (IRRs) for each partnership with and without the use of credit facility. Please note if the IRRs are not net.
7.	Investment multiple (TV/PI) for each individual partnership.
8.	The dollar amount of “total management fees and costs paid” for each individual partnership.
9.	Date as of which all the above data was calculated.
10.	Names of all alternative asset partnerships partially and fully sold by City of Kissimmee Municipal Firefighters' Retirement Plan, including date of sale.
11.	For each fund, please indicate whether or not the fund uses Subscription Credit Facilities.
I also request a copy of any disclosable documents which contain some or all of the following information:
12.	Names of all hedge fund holdings (including hedge fund of funds) in City of Kissimmee Municipal Firefighters' Retirement Plan's portfolio.
13.	Month by Month Market Value for each hedge fund holding (including hedge fund of funds) since City of Kissimmee Municipal Firefighters' Retirement Plan's initial investment up to  2Q26.
14.	Month by Month Contributions to each hedge fund holding (including hedge fund of funds) since City of Kissimmee Municipal Firefighters' Retirement Plan's initial investment up to 2Q26.
15.	Month by Month Returns (net of fees) earned by City of Kissimmee Municipal Firefighters' Retirement Plan for each hedge fund holding (including hedge fund of funds) since initial investment up to 2Q26.
If there are any fees for searching for, reviewing, or copying the records, please inform me before you task the request. If you deny all or any part of this request, please cite each specific exemption you think justifies your refusal to release the information and notify me of appeal procedures available under the law.
16. Investment memorandum used by the City of Kissimmee Municipal Firefighters' Retirement Plan investment committee and investment consultants providing consultation to the City of Kissimmee Municipal Firefighters' Retirement Plan private equity, venture capital, mezzanine, distressed, real estate/REIT, debt and infrastructure partnerships being considered for investment by the City of Kissimmee Municipal Firefighters' Retirement Plan portfolio.
17. All due diligence materials and presentation materials produced by the General Partners in the course of the City of Kissimmee Municipal Firefighters' Retirement Plan conducting due diligence on investments into any private equity, venture capital, mezzanine, distressed, real estate/REIT, debt, and infrastructure partnerships.
18. For each fund, please indicate whether or not the fund uses Subscription Credit Facilities.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Kelly Lyles

title: Minneapolis and St. Paul Police - LexisNexis / AVCC Data Sharing (Minneapolis Police Department)

communications.subject: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: Minneapolis and St. Paul Police - LexisNexis / AVCC Data Sharing (Minneapolis Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act, I hereby request the following records:

REQUEST: Please provide all emails between employees of your police department and LexisNexis from October 1, 2025 through July 28, 2026. You may de-duplicate emails if the same email was sent to multiple employees. Please include attachments. Please ensure the responsive emails and documents are preserved during the time it takes to process this request. The LexisNexis email domains are @LexisNexisRisk.com and @LexisNexis.com 

CONTEXT: During Operation Metro Surge, LexisNexis wrote an email stating that they hope to soon have data from Minneapolis Police and St. Paul Police available to subscribers of Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC). LexisNexis has AVCC contracts with, and sells data access to ICE, the Navy, the VA, the DOJ, and 2,400 federal and local agencies around the U.S., meaning they can view victim and witness details of police reports and 911 calls from departments that allow LexisNexis to copy their data. We are trying to understand whether your agency has started sharing your CAD/RMS data with federal agencies via LexisNexis's AVCC / Public Safety Data Exchange (PSDEx).

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

title: Use of force data collection (2025) (Irving Police Department)

communications.subject: Texas Public Information Act Request: Use of force data collection (2025) (Irving Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Use of force (UOF) data dating from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025. If possible, please provide this data in database or spreadsheet format and include the case number, incident date, incident time, subject injured indicator, subject injury force related info (e.g. Yes or No), subject age, subject gender, subject race/ethnicity, subject weapon type, incident location, area occurred, force type, officer division (e.g. law enforcement operations, detention/correctional operations, etc.), badge number and names associated with the officers involved. If one or more of these fields is unavailable, provide all fields and/or information that is available responsive to my request. If no database or spreadsheet format is available, please provide copies of each individual use of force report or other report where use of force information is documented/reported by officers. Note, this is for all use of force incidents reported by your agency, not limited to only those incidents required to be reported under state or federal programs.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Samuel Sinyangwe

title: Itemized Fee Petitions, Invoices, and Settlement Payouts (McMinimee Law)

communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: Itemized Fee Petitions, Invoices, and Settlement Payouts (McMinimee Law)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. All itemized invoices, line-item billing sheets, and fee petitions submitted to Vancouver Public Schools, its legal counsel, its board of directors, or its risk-management carriers by Shannon McMinimee or any agent operating under the domain or entity name "McMinimee Law".
2. All transactional records, ledger entries, checks, voucher approvals, board warrant registry items, or electronic funds transfer records documenting attorney fee payouts, cost reimbursements, or financial settlement distributions paid directly to McMinimee Law or Shannon McMinimee, specifically including but not limited to the $9,000.00 check/warrant processed on or around March 10, 2026 under Account Code 10 E 530 9700.
3. The chronological scope of this request spans from January 4, 2022, through June 30, 2025, specifically targeting all billing blocks, settlement agreements, and fee recovery actions generated while the attorney was concurrently operating under private credentials and public employment contracts.

PRE-EMPTIVE STATUTORY ENFORCEMENT & COMPLIANCE CLAUSE:
The District is advised that, per Washington law (Progressive Animal Welfare Soc. v. University of Wash.), attorney billing records for public payment are subject to disclosure. Only specific, narrow redactions (e.g., student names under FERPA) are permitted, as blanket privilege claims are invalid under Soter v. Cowles Publishing Co.

MANDATORY STATUTORY COMPLIANCE TIMELINE:
A response is expected within five business days as per RCW 42.56.520. The records, requested for non-commercial purposes, should be provided electronically.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting

communications.subject: RE: Washington Public Records Act Request #R001116-080326
communications.communication:
Dear Jen Anderson,

Thank you for the general ledger entries provided on August 31, 2026. While the District has provided basic accounting records proving Check No. 415420 was processed, the response remains non-compliant with the full scope of the request under the Washington Public Records Act (PRA). I object to the administrative closure of this request based on the following deficiencies:

1. Item 1 (Line-Item Billing Sheets): Page 19 contains only a flat summary sheet referencing a block of 30.0 hours. Under Progressive Animal Welfare Society (PAWS) v. University of Washington, 125 Wash. 2d 243 (1994), attorney billing sheets and time blocks documenting public expenditures are public records subject to disclosure. Please produce the actual itemized time logs, dates, and detailed line-item billing entries submitted by McMinimee Law to justify the $10,500 total expenditure.

2. Item 2 (Over-Redaction of Settlement Agreement): Pages 8, 9, and 10 of the produced settlement contract are entirely blacked out. Under Soter v. Cowles Publishing Co., 162 Wash. 2d 716 (2007) and RCW 42.56.210(1), blanket page-level withholdings are structurally unlawful. While the District must redact specific student-identifiable elements protected by FERPA, it is legally required to segment the record, leaving the systemic contractual terms, general operational agreements, and non-identifiable text fully visible. 

Please provide a revised, properly parsed production of the settlement agreement and the missing detailed time logs to satisfy this request.

Respectfully Submitted in the Public Interest,

Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: CVISS Member Agencies - LexisNexis/Accurint Data Sharing Agreements (Elk Grove Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

1) All MOUs, contracts, addendums, or other legal documents signed by your agency and LexisNexis (and subsidiaries, including LexisNexis Risk Solutions, Accurint, AVCC, PSDEX, etc.). This may include (but is not limited to) a LexisNexis Consortium Sub-Agency Addendum, Schedule A, or other agreements.
2) Any MOUs or other agreements between your agency and CVISS or Sacramento County Sheriff related to sharing RMS/CAD data.
3) Agency Configuration Page: A printout of your agency's AVCC configuration page. Please include the full page, including any other agencies listed on the same page. Example Screenshot: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1G_J35fnmu7qZO_k8UOoVHFcd_R2HKXVg/view?usp=sharing

Context: We understand that CVISS moved to the LexisNexis Accurint platform to share data among CVISS member agencies. We are seeking to understand whether your agency and other CVISS members share contributed data with agencies beyond the consortium (e.g., the Public Safety Data Exchange / PSDEX national database), or whether data sharing is restricted to CVISS members only. Often LexisNexis Sub-Agency Addendums allow agencies to choose whether they share nationally or only within the consortium - we seek to understand what your agency chose to do.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records related to Treasury OIG investigation DO-23-0085-I.

Specifically, I request:
1 ) The final Report of Investigation (ROI) or any closing report summarizing findings
2) Any closing memorandum, investigative summary, or substantiation determination
3) Records reflecting any disciplinary, administrative, or corrective actions taken as a result of the investigation
4) Any referrals to the Department of Justice or other agencies
5) Policies, guidance, or internal assessments generated or modified as a result of this investigation

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Public records regarding Magic School, Inc. and Brisk Teaching, Inc.
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act (Government Code § 7920.000 et seq.), I request copies of the following records. Where records exist in electronic form, I request them in their native electronic format. I request that responsive records be produced on a rolling basis as they are identified, rather than withheld until all records have been compiled.



1. The MagicSchool Enterprise Contract and Related Agreements

a) The fully executed agreement(s) between the District and Magic School, Inc. corresponding to Quote Number 00007419 / Requisition RQ27-00068, approved by the Board of Trustees on June 10, 2026 (Agenda Item 11.37), including all attachments, exhibits, and order forms.

b) Any prior contract, order form, quote, or agreement between the District and Magic School, Inc. covering the period from August 2025 through June 2026 (i.e., preceding the 2026/27 Enterprise agreement), including any agreement under which the Fall 2025 pilot and the announced March 2026 adoption operated.

c) Any invoices or payment records issued to or by the District in connection with either agreement described above.

2. Data Processing Agreement

All Data Processing Agreements (DPAs), data privacy addenda, or "custom DPA" documents referenced in the MagicSchool Enterprise quote description (Quote Number 00007419), whether in draft or executed form, between the District and Magic School, Inc. If no DPA has been executed as of the date of this request, please confirm that in your response.

3. Procurement Process and Communications

a) All electronic communications, including emails and attachments, between any District employee using a @seq.org email address — including but not limited to Barbara Reklis (breklis@seq.org) and Dr. Elizabeth Chacón — and any representative of Magic School, Inc., including but not limited to Kristy Klare (kristy@magicschool.ai), from January 1, 2025 to the date of this request.

b) Any requisition records, purchase requisitions, or procurement approval documents associated with Requisition Number RQ27-00068.

c) Any internal District policy, administrative regulation, or board policy establishing a dollar threshold above which a purchase requires individual board discussion as opposed to placement on a consent agenda, and any record reflecting whether Agenda Item 11.37 (June 10, 2026) was discussed individually or approved solely as part of the consent agenda.

4. AI Working Group Records

All records related to the "AI working group" described in the District's March 2026 board presentation (Agenda Item 14.2) as launching in Spring 2026, including: recruitment announcements or invitations; rosters or lists of participants, including their role or title (e.g., teacher, administrator, student, parent, community member); meeting agendas, minutes, and materials; and any interim findings, draft guidelines, or draft policy language produced to date.

5. Enrollment and Licensing Basis

Any record identifying the basis for the license quantity of 8,666 units reflected in Quote Number 00007419, including but not limited to total district student enrollment figures used for licensing purposes, or any internal communication explaining how that quantity was determined.

6. Pilot Program Evaluation Records

All records related to the evaluation of the MagicSchool and Brisk Teaching pilot programs conducted during Fall 2025 (approximately August through November 2025), including: survey instruments and responses distributed to all teachers (redacted to remove individual teacher identifiers if necessary); evaluation rubrics or comparison criteria; and any summary report or memorandum documenting the rationale for selecting MagicSchool for district-wide adoption.

7. Parent and Student Notification Records

All records of notice provided to parents, guardians, or students regarding MagicSchool's use in District classrooms from June 1, 2025 to the date of this request, including consent or opt-out forms, notification letters or emails, and any records documenting the District's compliance with California Education Code § 49073.1 regarding disclosure of student information to third-party vendors.

8. Board Meeting Materials

The complete board agenda packet, staff report, and any supplementary materials associated with Agenda Item 11.37 from the June 10, 2026 regular board meeting, and Agenda Item 14.2 from the March 2026 board meeting, including any version of the MagicSchool quote or presentation slide deck not already publicly posted.



I am a student journalist with Scot Scoop, the student newspaper of Carlmont High School within the Sequoia Union High School District. This request is made in the public interest to inform the school community about the District's procurement of AI educational tools. As such, I respectfully request a waiver or reduction of any fees associated with this request.

Because I am requesting electronic copies of these records in their native format, I expect there to be no fees associated with this request pursuant to Gov. Code § 7922.570. If the estimated cost of producing these records exceeds $50, please notify me before proceeding so that I may narrow the request if necessary.

I request a determination on disclosability within 10 calendar days as required by Government Code § 7922.535. If you determine that any portion of the requested records is exempt from disclosure, please redact only those portions and provide the remainder of the record. For any redaction or denial, please cite the specific legal exemption justifying the withholding, as required by Government Code § 7922.540.

Thank you for your attention to this request.

Sincerely,
Maximus Kwan

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Pay Per Clique
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

This request is being submitted under the following statutes FOIA
FFATA and DATA. 

Request for records within the Federal Bureau of Investigation, related to spending on the rollout of the 'what qualifies as a hate crime and how to report one.'

I was seeking the following:

Copies of any records of News Media sites that were targeted with pay-per-click advertising including but not limited to the www.dailymail.uk.

Copies of any internal memoranda including  but not limited to discussions of ramifications of potentially favorable news coverage and improved media relations due to the spending campaign

Copies of all contracts for advertising

Copies of accounting for all monies spent for pay per click advertising as of the date of the request.

A portion of this campeign was recently cited in the news:
https://www.stltoday.com/news/local/crime-and-courts/fbi-rolls-out-ad-campaign-to-encourage-hate-crime-reporting/article_1aa68b2e-2e89-566e-b372-87bf25cbf764.html

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

William Fernandes

The FBI's FOIPA Program is searching the FBI's indices for potentially responsive documents.

title: FBI support for TV docuseries "The Case Of: JonBenet Ramsey" (2016)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FBI support for TV docuseries "The Case Of: JonBenet Ramsey" (2016)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All documents pertaining to FBI support for or collaboration with the production of the TV docuseries "The Case Of: JonBenet Ramsey" (2016), directed by Eddie Schmidt. Such documents may include, but should not be limited to, script notes; production assistance agreements; photographs; and all records of communications between employees of the FBI and members of the cast, crew, and production company of "The Case Of: JonBenet Ramsey," including memos, notes of meetings and conference calls, emails, and other forms of communication. I request a search of all locations where such documents might be located, including but not limited to the entertainment liaison offices and communications HQ or similar offices.

I am the Director of Research Operations at a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization called The Decoding Culture Foundation. These documents will be used for public education and research purposes. I therefore request a waiver of all fees that may otherwise apply. Attached is a document with organization letterhead confirming my position, as well as the organization's 501(c)(3) application and approval form.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Brett Carollo

communications.subject: RE: Arizona Public Records Law Request: Hernandez emails
communications.communication:
Dear Mr. Riches,

Thank you for the records you produced on August 26 in response to my July 23 request for correspondence between the office of Rep. Alma Hernandez and addresses ending in *gov.il, *aipac.org, *aipacpac.org, *jewishinsider.com, and *standwithus.com, for the period beginning October 1, 2024.

I've now reviewed all four PDFs. Before I treat the production as final, would you please confirm whether it is complete — and, if so, help me understand several results that appear inconsistent with the scope of the request?

1. Three of the five domains returned nothing. The production contains no records from or to any address at aipac.org, aipacpac.org, or standwithus.com. Was each of these domains in fact searched, and did each return zero results?

2. The production contains no outbound email. My request covered emails sent from Rep. Hernandez's office to these domains as well as emails sent to it. Every record produced is inbound. Please confirm whether the Sent Items folder (and any equivalent) was searched, and whether the search was constructed to capture outbound messages.

3. Almost nothing predates June 2026. The request covered roughly twenty-one months. Of the approximately thirty-six messages produced, all but three are Jewish Insider newsletters, and the welcome message in the production (file 4, p. 112) shows that subscription began on June 17, 2026. The only records produced from before that date are three emails from the Consulate General of Israel in Los Angeles, all dated July 8, 2025. If the office genuinely exchanged no other email with these five domains between October 1, 2024 and June 2026, I will accept that. But I'd like to rule out the alternative first.

4. Additional Consulate correspondence likely exists. Published accounts of the "50 States, One Israel" delegation indicate that five legislators per state were invited. The production contains three Arizona invitations — to Rep. Michael Way, Sen. Eva Diaz, and Rep. Kevin Volk — each copied to Rep. Hernandez. If additional invitations were sent to or copied to her office, or if she received an invitation addressed to her directly, those would be responsive and do not appear in the production. So would any reply, RSVP, or subsequent correspondence with the Consulate about the delegation.

5. Redaction. In all three Consulate emails, a phone number has been removed from the body text without any notation or exemption cited. If information was withheld, please identify what was withheld and the legal basis for withholding it, so that I can evaluate it.

To help me determine whether items 1–4 reflect true absences or the design of the search, please tell me:

Which mailboxes and accounts were searched, and for which custodians;
What search terms or method were used (domain-level search, keyword, manual review);
Whether archived mail, deleted items, and any journaling or backup system were included;
Whether any non-legislative account or device used for official correspondence was within scope, and if not, whether the office has represented that none was used;
What retention schedule applies to legislative email, and whether any responsive records were deleted or overwritten during the request period.

I'm not asking you to create records that don't exist. If the answer for any of these is that a complete search was run and returned nothing, please say so plainly. I'd simply rather establish that now than assume it. Thank you again for your work on this.

Sincerely,
Matthew Petti

communications.subject: RE: Arizona Public Records Law Request: Hernandez emails
communications.communication:
Hi Matthew,
Thank you for your email.  We can confirm that the production is final and that our office searched Alma Hernandez's account for inbound and outbound emails in the date range of October 1, 2024 to July 23, 2026.  Specifically, we searched for all communications (to, from, CC, BCC) with the following domains: @gov.il, @aipac.org, @aipacpac.org, @jewishinsider.com and @standwithus.com.  Additionally, we can confirm that there were no outbound results and all communications captured by the search were inbound.  Regarding question 5, a phone number in the body of the email appeared to be a personal cell phone, so it was redacted for privacy reasons.
If you have any other questions or we can assist you with anything else, please don't hesitate to contact us.
Best regards,
Justin Riches
Public Records Counsel
(602) 926-5507

communications.subject: Indiana Access to Public Records Act Request: Bernard Myers (Tippecanoe County Sheriff)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Indiana Access to Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records related to the following current or former employees:

Bernard Myers

Hiring date, termination date, compensation, commendations, assignments/job roles, disciplinary actions, factual basis for disciplinary actions and letters of resignation for the following employees. Please exclude copies of individual training certificates.

I am including the following information as a helpful reference to related case law and Public Access Counselor opinions regarding personnel records of public employees:

Indiana Supreme Court decision WTHR-TV v. Hamilton Southeastern School District states that APRA requires disclosure of the factual basis for disciplinary action, and that factual basis cannot be a bald conclusion. It also has to be sufficient for a reasonable person to understand what an employee did to deserve discipline. See the opinion starting on page 7 of the link above.

A passing reference to violation of a specific policy is not sufficient to meet this standard.

The Indiana Public Access Counselor also has addressed the topic of resignations in lieu of termination. One such opinion can be reviewed here, but simply put a resignation in lieu of a termination does not dissolve an agency’s responsibility to provide the factual basis for discipline under the public records statute.

The state’s records statute applies to all employees, regardless of wither they are probationary or not.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emily Hopkins

communications.communication:
Dear e e: 
Thank you for submitting a records request to the City of Charleston Police Department to be processed under the South Carolina Freedom of Information Act (FOIA). Your request was received on July 28, 2026, and is being processed in accordance with S.C. Code Ann. § 30-4-10, et seq. Your request has been assigned the reference number L026683-072826 for tracking purposes. 
Records Requested: To Whom It May Concern: 

Pursuant to the South Carolina Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records: 

- All contracts, licenses, MOUs, MOAs, data agreements, letters of intent, State of Work documents, Scope of Work documents, and other agreement documents with Axon Enterprise that were active any time between 1/1/2023 and 7/29/2026. 

- All financial documents or records of financial transactions, exchanges or obligations related to Axon Enterprise dated between 1/1/2023 and 7/29/2026. Responsive materials include all invoices, bills, receipts, check stubs, or any other records, including those possessed in an electronic format. 

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. 

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not. 

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 15 business days, as the statute requires. 

Sincerely, 

Upload documents directly: https://www.muckrock.com/respond/2353853/ 
The City of Charleston Police Department will provide a formal acknowledgment within 10 business days informing you of the availability of the non-exempt “public records” that you have requested and providing a time and cost estimate to make those public records available to you. For records more than 24 months old, the City has 20 business days to respond on availability and cost. We do not guarantee that a records search will result in any responsive records being located. 
Fulfillment of FOIA requests is subject to fees for search, retrieval and redaction, as well as fees for providing copies of documents. A deposit of twenty-five (25%) percent of the total reasonably anticipated cost for fulfilling the request may be required prior to searching for or making copies of records. The full amount of the total cost must be paid at the time of the production of the request. 
If the request is granted, the records will be furnished or made available for inspection or copying no later than thirty (30) calendar days from the date on which the formal acknowledgement was provided, unless the records are more than two (2) years old, in which case they will be made available no later than thirty-five (35) calendar days from the date on which the formal acknowledgement was provided. If a deposit is required, the records will be furnished or made available for inspection or copying no later than thirty (30) calendar days from the date on which the deposit is received, unless the records are more than two (2) years old, in which case they will be made available no later than thirty-five (35) calendar days from the date on which the deposit was received to fulfill the request. The Charleston Police Department may impose reasonable rules concerning time and place of access to records. 
* Please note that pursuant to S.C. Code Ann. §30-2-50, obtaining or using public records for commercial solicitation directed to any person in this State is prohibited. A person who knowingly violates this section is guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction, must be fined an amount not to exceed five hundred dollars or imprisoned for a term not to exceed one year, or both. 
We do not make public, and will not produce in response to your request, those records that are exempt from disclosure under S.C. Code Ann. § 30-4-40 or other state and federal laws. 
 
You can monitor the progress of your request at the FOIA Records Request Center. You'll receive a formal acknowledgment e-mail from the City within 10 business days (or within 20 business days for records more than 24 months old) when availability and cost have been determined. 
Sincerely, 
Charleston Police Department

title: Housing Demand by Bedroom Count

communications.subject: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: Housing Demand by Bedroom Count
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oklahoma Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

An electronic copy of the most recent existing report, spreadsheet, database export, or similar electronic record showing Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) demand by bedroom size.

Specifically, I am seeking the number of applicants, waiting-list households, voucher holders, or assisted households by required bedroom size, such as 1-bedroom, 2-bedroom, 3-bedroom, 4-bedroom, and larger units.

If this information is already maintained by county, ZIP code, city, or another geographic area, please include that geographic breakdown.

Excel, CSV, or the record's native electronic format is preferred.

I am not requesting personally identifiable information.

To minimize staff time and costs, I am requesting existing electronic records or an existing database export only. I am not asking OHFA to create a new report, perform calculations, or conduct additional analysis.

If fulfilling this request would require more than two hours of staff time or result in any fees, please provide an estimate before performing the additional work.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

AJ Keys

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Records retention schedule (Nuclear Regulatory Commission)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Any and all materials, indices, directives, manuals, and other guiding documentation regarding records generated and retained, including but not limited to: 

• Record retention schedules
• Any other data structures used for the management of records: digital, paper, and otherwise

I request that you release records for this request on a rolling basis as they become available and in electronic form. If your agency does not maintain these public records, please let me know who does and include the proper custodian's name and address. If you choose to deny this request, please provide a written explanation for the denial including a reference to the specific statutory exemption(s) upon which you rely. Also, please provide all segregable portions of otherwise exempt material.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. 

Sincerely,

Dillon Bergin

title: HCV Contract Rents

communications.subject: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: HCV Contract Rents
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oklahoma Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

an electronic copy of the most recent existing report, spreadsheet, database export, or similar electronic record showing approved Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) contract rents.

Specifically, I am seeking approved contract rent amounts along with bedroom count and the property's ZIP code, city, county, or other geographic area already maintained in the record.

If readily available within the same existing record, please also include the effective date of the approved rent.

Excel, CSV, or the record's native electronic format is preferred.

I am not requesting tenant names or other personally identifiable information.

To minimize staff time and costs, I am requesting existing electronic records or an existing database export only. I am not asking OHFA to create a new report, perform calculations, or conduct additional analysis.

If fulfilling this request would require more than two hours of staff time or result in any fees, please provide an estimate before performing the additional work.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

AJ Keys

title: FOIA - FBI - Chandler Davis

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: FOIA - FBI - Chandler Davis
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All records mentioning Chandler Davis (August 12, 1926 - September 24, 2022) - American-Canadian mathematician, writer, teacher, and activist (see: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandler_Davis )

Please conduct a thorough search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices - for both main-file records and cross-reference records for all relevant names, individuals, agencies and companies. 

If any potentially responsive records have been destroyed and/or transferred to NARA, then I request copies of the destruction or transfer slips as well as any other documentation relating to, mentioning or describing said transfer or destruction, to include but not be limited to confirmation that the Bureau has no other copies of said records. If previously released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed for release.

Please see the following news publication to serve as proof of death: https://www.tabletmag.com/sections/history/articles/the-purge-chandler-davis

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

J Ader

communications.communication:
Thank you for contacting foipaquestions@fbi.gov.  Please check the status of your FOIPA Request at http://vault.fbi.gov by clicking on "Check Status of Your FOI/PA Request" on the right side of the page, and follow the instructions below.

Check the Status of Your FOIPA Request
If your FOIPA Number is [1234567-0] please enter [1234567-000] into the system. If your FOIPA Number is [1234567-1] please enter [1234567-001] into the system. If you have any questions about the status of your FOIPA request, please e-mail foipaquestions@fbi.gov.

FIND STATUS OF FOIPA- Request statuses are updated weekly

Please enter the whole FOIPA number-Example: [1234567-000]

FOIPA:
Results will show the Request Number, Case Type and Process Description shown below:
FOIPA:
1234567-000

Case Type:
FOIPA

Process Description (Will display the current progress of the request)
The FBI's FOIPA Program is searching the FBI's indices for potentially responsive documents.
You may be contacted via formal letter for all fees and/or negotiation issues that may apply.

NOTE: Recent requests are entered into the FOIPA database in the order that they are received. Before you can check the status, you must have received correspondence assigning a FOIPA request number and the information transferred to the online database. Status information is updated weekly. If a request has been closed within the last six months the online database will display the following: The FOIPA number entered has been closed, and appropriate correspondence has been sent to the address on file.

Estimated Dates of Completion
Requests are processed in the order in which they are received through our multi-track processing system.  Requests are divided into two primary tracks--simple (under 50 pages of potentially responsive documents) and complex (over 50 pages of potentially responsive documents).  Complex requests are further divided into medium, large, and extra-large sub-tracks based upon request size.  Simple track requests typically require the least amount of time to process.  Currently, simple track cases average approximately 98 days from the date of receipt for processing.  Our complex requests in the medium processing track are currently averaging 947 days, large processing track are currently averaging approximately 2,011 days, and extra-large processing track are currently averaging 2,360 days for processing.

Respectfully,

Public Information Officer
FBI - Information Management Division
200 Constitution Drive
Winchester, VA  22602
O: (540) 868-4593
E: foipaquestions@fbi.gov<mailto:foipaquestions@fbi.gov>

Do you have further questions about the FOI/PA process? Visit us at http://www.fbi.gov/foia

Please check the status of your request online at https://vault.fbi.gov/fdps-1/@@search-fdps    Status updates are performed on a weekly basis.

Note:  This is a non-emergency email address.  If this is an emergency, please call 911 directly.  If you need to report a tip for immediate action, please contact FBI Tips at http://tips.fbi.gov/ or reach out to your local field office.

title: George Blake (Federal Bureau of Investigation)

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: George Blake (Federal Bureau of Investigation)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records mentioning or describing George Blake. I request that any pre-processed records be provided initially, with additional records being provided on a rolling basis.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Emma North-Best

communications.communication:
# Individual Information

Prefix First Name Middle Name Last Name Suffix Email Phone Location
